note: v3351: The total-window ratchet went 60 to 50 against a ceiling of 44, silent stays 0, and test_control passed 2,238 tests after every conversion. TEN fixed-size source windows now end where their subject ends, via two helpers: _py_fn_around (ast, the innermost function CONTAINING the anchor) and _js_fn_from (brace-balanced from the anchor). The headline pair was measured, not guessed: toggleTooltipPass is 6,814 chars and its guard read 12,000, reaching 5,186 chars into the NEXT function where an innocent match would satisfy a positive assertIn and pass GREEN falsely; vaultAccumApply is 41,387 and its guard read 30,000, never seeing the last 28%. ⚠⚠ TWO CONVERSIONS WERE MADE AND THEN REVERTED BECAUSE THE MEASUREMENT REFUTED THEM, AND THAT REFINES THE RULE: a real boundary only beats a byte count when it is a TIGHTER one. _tick(reopenedReels= sits inside a 51,705-char function, so bounding to it would widen the read 36x - and with silent now 0 every remaining window is under a POSITIVE assertion, where OVER-reach is the silent direction and under-reach merely fails loudly. board_ownership( sits at MODULE level, so the helper returns empty and the converted guard would have asserted over an empty string. Both now carry a comment saying the byte window is deliberate, which is the difference between a window nobody examined and one somebody decided about. ⚠⚠⚠ THE CROSS-FAMILY EYE FOUND TWO REAL LATENT DEFECTS IN THE HELPER v3350 SHIPPED, AND BOTH ARE FIXED HERE: taking the FIRST ast.walk match picks an arbitrary call site the moment a callee repeats, because walk yields DFS and not source order - a NEGATIVE assertion would then be handed a window describing a different call; and the body search returned on its first hit, which a one-line if-colon-call makes ambiguous. Reproduced before believing: 1 call site and 1 matching body today, so both were LATENT rather than live. Fixed by collecting every candidate and REFUSING unless exactly one, which is what the helper already promised for every other failure. 475 gates, test_control[0] PROVEN.
